editorial:
Imagine spending your whole life running away from a childhood you can't quite remember, only to realize that the past is still waiting for you. You follow a young man who goes back to his old hometown to fix some old mistakes, but he quickly finds out that his memories aren't what they seem. The vibe is a mix of a sad family drama and a weird fantasy trip. It feels like a dream where things are slightly off, and you spend most of the movie trying to piece together the puzzle along with the main character as he deals with a part of himself he tried to hide for years.

The acting is solid and makes you really feel the pain of the lead character. While the story moves a bit slow at times, the emotional payoff at the end makes it worth your while. If you like movies that make you think about your own life and secrets, you will love this. Since it has some beautiful shots, you should try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best experience. If you prefer owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great way to keep this one.
endingExplained: You find out that the main character has been dealing with a split personality caused by childhood trauma. The fantasy elements were actually his mind trying to process grief and guilt. In the final scenes, he finally accepts the hidden part of himself and stops running. He makes peace with his past and decides to live honestly. It ends with him feeling whole again, knowing that the truth is the only way to truly heal.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about memory and healing.
